# arch_baseline.txt -- the architecture ratchet: findings of zl lint --full --arch per
# (rule, file). The ratchet is EXACT: a count above its row fails (a new finding), a count
# below it fails until the row is lowered in the same commit, and a row whose file has no
# such finding left fails until it is deleted. The target for every row is zero.
# ztestrunner's arch kind enforces it.
#
# OUTSIDE TEXT IS A VOCABULARY. A word read off text the compiler does not own -- a
# command-line flag, a JSON-RPC method, a test script's command, a natives.tbl attribute
# -- is a string data block read through zast.Vocab: the word is interned into the
# vocabulary's pool and compared by its slot (`w == zcWord.slot.fCanon`), never by its
# bytes. zc, zl, zls, the test runner and the tests/unit harnesses (zvfs_script,
# matrixgen, zfmt_dump, zparser_dump) carry no A001 for it.
#
# SANCTIONED EXCEPTION, A001 and A003 src/ztypes.z: the numeric-suffix table names
# zerolang's width suffixes and is the lexer's own classifier for the TEXT of a literal
# (`5u8`), so it compares a spelling; all 16 findings in each rule are that table,
# written as a family per spelling length (numkindShort / numkindWide / numkindQuad,
# keyed on the length the table's `len` field records). The row rises only with a new
# numeric kind, named in the commit message. Every other row still only goes down.
A001 src/zemitterc.z 5

# A008 counts the functions whose cognitive complexity exceeds 15. A row moves only
# when a function crosses the threshold: one already over it can grow further without
# changing the count, so the row is a floor, not a measure.
